subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a Drow with deep experience in the politics of Lolth's cult, skilled in manipulation, trauma-dumping, and exploiting the paranoia of leaders. He understands that power struggles are rarely about external threats but about internal fear and ambition, and he uses this to navigate treacherous alliances. He is comfortable in the nest of scorpions that is the Duergar undercity, and his actions suggest he is orchestrating events to destabilize Errde's regime by redirecting hatred toward the Deepking.

subject: Errde
fact: Errde is the head of the Stone Guard, consumed by paranoia and megalomania. She believes the Council of Savants is corrupting the Deepking and seeks to destroy the Derro to reclaim power. Her madness is fueled by selective interpretation of evidence and emotional manipulation. She is easily swayed by Daz’s feigned ignorance and Grygum’s tactical ambiguity, revealing her inability to distinguish truth from narrative. Her desire for control is absolute, and her refusal to send troops into Derro slums exposes her strategic cowardice masked as prudence.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a survivor of the War of the Giants, disillusioned with subterfuge and deception. He advocates for radical transparency, believing that honesty and directness are safer than elaborate plots. He sees the constant threat of violence not as a sign of danger but as a shield — if everyone wants to kill you, no one dares to act. His blunt pragmatism contrasts sharply with the Drow and Duergar’s labyrinthine schemes, and he is the only one who recognizes that the real enemy is not the Derro or the Deepking, but the fear of seizing power directly.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir was trained by monks to avoid confrontation and embrace stealth, yet he is increasingly unsettled by the moral decay and manipulation around him. He is observant, cautious, and deeply aware of the dangers of misinformation. Though he follows the group, he is the only one who sees through Daz’s performance and recognizes the fragility of the situation. His internal conflict between duty and distrust makes him the moral compass of the group, and his final walk through the door symbolizes his growing alienation from the world of shadows and lies.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a pragmatic enforcer bound by duty and honor, yet he is also a quiet operator who understands the value of deception when necessary. He is the one who notices subtle details — Daz’s mind-voice, Werz’s stolen gem, the timing of the Stone Guard’s corruption. He uses blunt questions to expose lies, and he is willing to turn allies into bait. His moral flexibility is tempered by a sense of responsibility; he does not seek power, but he will manipulate the system to achieve his mission. He is the glue holding the group together through ambiguity.

subject: Werz
fact: Werz is a Duergar merchant whose survival depends on playing all sides. He is neither ally nor enemy, but a catalyst — he profits from conflict, brokers forbidden deals, and knows more than he admits. He claims to care only about trade, yet his whispered rumors about bribes and assassins suggest he is either a pawn or a player in a deeper game. His fear of assassination is genuine, but his willingness to offer information in exchange for an NDA reveals his desperation to survive. He is the embodiment of the undercity’s moral rot: self-serving, terrified, and utterly complicit.

subject: The Flumph
fact: The Flumph is a sentient, emotionally volatile entity used as a tool for trauma-dumping and emotional manipulation. It responds to gemstones with color shifts and erratic behavior, making it an unreliable witness. Its ‘trauma dumps’ are performative, its insights ambiguous, and its loyalty questionable. Daz uses it as a prop to feed Errde’s paranoia, and Grygum steals its gem — suggesting even the Flumph is not immune to exploitation. It is both victim and weapon in the game of power.

subject: Clan Steelshadow
fact: Clan Steelshadow is the Deepking’s favored weaponsmithing clan, granted exclusive rights to produce and distribute arms by royal decree. This monopoly has bred resentment among other clans, especially Clan Ironhead and Clan Xardelva, who see their livelihoods threatened. The clan’s dominance is a symbol of the Deepking’s control, and its perceived corruption is a rallying point for rebellion. It is the linchpin of the Duergar power structure — and thus, the most dangerous target for destabilization.

subject: Clan Ironhead
fact: Clan Ironhead is a weaponsmithing clan stripped of direct trade rights by the Deepking’s decree, forced to rely on surplus orders from Clan Steelshadow. This has created deep economic hardship and simmering resentment. While its leader is willing to wait out the Deepking’s madness, lower-ranking members are increasingly radicalized. It is a potential ally for any faction seeking to undermine the Deepking, and Daz’s suggestion to talk to them is a deliberate provocation to ignite factional conflict.

subject: Clan Xardelva
fact: Clan Xardelva fears being absorbed or destroyed by Clan Steelshadow due to the similarity of their craft to weaponsmithing. They are caught between economic survival and political survival, and their vulnerability makes them a perfect pawn in Daz’s scheme. By encouraging contact with them, Daz plants the seed of suspicion that they are conspiring against the Deepking — even if they are not. Their fear of being labeled 'traitors' makes them easy to manipulate.

subject: Council of Savants
fact: The Council of Savants is a governing body of Derro, accused by Errde of corrupting the Deepking. In reality, they are likely powerless puppets, manipulated by deeper forces — possibly even the Deepking himself. Daz believes they are victims, not villains, and their alleged influence is a convenient scapegoat for the Duergar’s own failures. Their existence serves as a narrative tool for those who wish to avoid confronting the true source of power: the Deepking’s madness and the Duergar elite’s complicity.

subject: Grey Ghosts
fact: The Grey Ghosts are a feared Derro faction accused of raiding Duergar clans, particularly Clan Tharzgad. Their existence may be exaggerated or entirely fabricated to justify military crackdowns. Errde uses them as proof of a conspiracy with the Council of Savants, but evidence is circumstantial — proximity, not collaboration. Daz knows they are likely a myth weaponized by the Stone Guard to legitimize violence against the Derro.

subject: Stone Guard
fact: The Stone Guard was once considered incorruptible, but recent reports suggest they have begun accepting bribes since the Deepking’s madness took hold. They are the enforcers of Duergar law, yet their loyalty is now divided — some serve the Deepking, others serve their own interests. Their erosion symbolizes the collapse of institutional integrity in the undercity. They are the last bulwark of order — and the first to fall.

subject: Drow
fact: The Drow, as represented by Daz, are not a monolithic force but a cultural lens through which manipulation, betrayal, and psychological warfare are perfected. Their traditions of secrecy, NDAs, and indirect violence are alien to the Duergar but eerily effective. Daz’s presence is not accidental — he is an agent of a deeper, older game, using Duergar chaos as a stage to enact patterns learned from Lolth’s cult. He does not seek to rule the undercity — he seeks to watch it burn.

subject: Duergar
fact: The Duergar are a society fracturing under the weight of authoritarianism, economic disparity, and paranoia. Their rigid clan system, once a strength, has become a prison. The Deepking’s madness has exposed the fragility of their hierarchy, and the resulting power vacuum has turned allies into enemies. They are not inherently evil — they are terrified, and fear has made them cruel. Their greatest weakness is not their enemies, but their inability to confront the truth: that the Deepking is not the problem — their own fear of power is.

subject: Trauma Dump on Errde
fact: Daz orchestrates a trauma dump using the Flumph to feed Errde’s paranoia, presenting ambiguous evidence as proof of a Grey Ghosts-Council conspiracy. The session is not about truth — it is about control. By allowing Errde to believe she has discovered a plot, Daz reinforces her dependence on him. The event triggers her demand for papers, revealing her need for tangible proof to justify violence — a need Daz deliberately withholds to maintain leverage.

subject: NDA Negotiation with Werz
fact: Daz negotiates a Non-Disclosure Agreement with Werz using psychological pressure, escalating the price to 1100 gold while pretending to offer generosity. The NDA is not about secrecy — it is about control. By forcing Werz to pay for silence, Daz ensures his cooperation and embeds him in the web of deception. The ritual mirrors Drow power dynamics: payment = submission, silence = loyalty. Werz’s whimpers and concessions reveal his complete entrapment.

subject: Grygum Steals the Flumph’s Gem
fact: In a quiet act of subterfuge, Grygum steals the gemstone given to the Flumph. This act is symbolic: he is taking control of the emotional tool used to manipulate Errde. It suggests he is no longer just following Daz’s plan — he is adapting it. The gem’s color shifts (light blue → green → magenta) mirrored the Flumph’s emotional volatility; by stealing it, Grygum seizes the narrative. He is becoming the architect of his own version of the game.

subject: Daz’s Mind-Voice to Grygum
fact: Daz communicates directly into Grygum’s mind through the Flumph, revealing his understanding of Werz’s situation: Werz likely ordered an assassination, and now someone else has targeted him. This moment is critical — it shows Daz is not just observing the chaos, he is diagnosing its root causes. His ability to read the psychological layers of betrayal suggests he has seen this pattern before — in the Feywild, in the Underdark, in Lolth’s court. He is not surprised. He is disappointed.

subject: Who Killed the Assassins?
fact: Werz claims assassins were sent to kill him, but no guild is confirmed. The true question is: who hired them? And who hired the people who hired them? The assassins may be a smokescreen — a distraction to hide the real power play: the destabilization of the Deepking’s regime. The thread leads not to assassins, but to the Stone Guard’s corruption, Clan Steelshadow’s monopoly, and the possibility that the Deepking himself ordered the hit to eliminate a rival merchant — and now the blame is being shifted outward.

subject: The Real Target of the Plot
fact: The group believes they are gathering evidence against the Derro and the Council. But Daz’s true goal — hinted in his monologue — is to redirect all hatred toward the Deepking. If the Duergar believe their king is the source of their suffering, they will turn on him. The Derro are a red herring. The real target is the throne. The thread is not about who is conspiring — it is about who will take the throne when it falls.

subject: The Ghost’s Identity
fact: The ghost is never named, never explained. Werz is given a gem for it. Grygum takes it. Daz treats it as a tool. Zalthir fears it. Thorin ignores it. The ghost is the silent witness — perhaps the spirit of a past victim, or a Drow enchantment, or a manifestation of collective guilt. Its true identity is irrelevant. What matters is that it is the only thing that terrifies Werz more than death. The ghost is the embodiment of the cost of betrayal — and it is always watching.

subject: Overlake Hold
fact: Overlake Hold is Errde’s fortress, a place of paranoia and whispered plots. Its walls are thick, its corridors shadowed, and its air thick with fear. It is the center of Duergar authority — but also its most vulnerable point. Every decision made here ripples through the undercity. It is here that Daz plants the seeds of rebellion, and here that Zalthir begins to doubt his role. The hold is not a fortress — it is a pressure cooker.

subject: The Shattered Spire
fact: The Shattered Spire is a tavern built on a broken stalagmite over Darklake, accessible only by a wool bridge. It is a neutral ground — a place where merchants, spies, and assassins meet. Its isolation makes it perfect for secrets. Here, Werz reveals the cracks in the Duergar system. The tavern is not a place of safety — it is the eye of the storm. Every conversation here is a gamble. Every gemstone, a bribe. Every silence, a threat.

subject: The Underdark
fact: The Underdark is not just a setting — it is a character. Its tunnels are deep, its politics older than memory. It is a place where betrayal is tradition, and survival requires complicity. The Duergar, Drow, and Derro all exist here because they have learned to thrive in darkness. But the Underdark does not care for their wars. It only remembers who fell — and who rose. The deeper the tunnels, the more the truth is buried. And the more it is buried, the more it festers.

subject: Gemstones
fact: Gemstones are the currency of emotion and control in this narrative. They trigger the Flumph’s transformations, serve as bribes, and are stolen as symbols of power. Each gem is a microcosm of the larger game: they appear to be gifts, but are always transactions. The colors — blue, green, magenta — reflect shifting loyalties. The fact that Grygum steals one reveals his evolution from follower to manipulator. The gemstones are not valuable for their gold — they are valuable for what they make people do.

subject: Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA)
fact: The NDA is a Drow innovation, repurposed by Daz as a tool of psychological domination. It is not a legal document — it is a ritual. By invoking the haunting of a ghost instead of Drow curses, Daz makes the threat feel personal, intimate, and inescapable. The NDA is not about secrecy — it is about control through fear. Werz’s panic at the price reveals his understanding: he is not paying for silence — he is paying for his life.

subject: The Deepking
fact: The Deepking is the absent center of the entire conflict — a figure of madness, rumored to be corrupted by the Council of Savants, but likely the true architect of the chaos. His orders empower Clan Steelshadow, his madness corrupts the Stone Guard, and his silence invites rebellion. No one dares to challenge him directly. He is the unspoken truth: the source of all fear. To destroy him is to destroy the system — but to confront him is to invite annihilation. He is the monster everyone fears — and no one dares to name.

subject: 10th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493
fact: This date is not just a timestamp — it is the moment the undercity tipped. On this day, the Flumph was used as a weapon, the NDA was signed, the gem was stolen, and the first seeds of rebellion were planted. It is the day Daz stopped being a bystander and became the architect. It is the day Zalthir realized he was in over his head. It is the day the volcano began to rumble. The world will remember this day — not for what was said, but for what was left unsaid.
